questions.title: In which country outside Iran, if any, will US forces strike Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026?
questions.background: Iran-aligned armed groups operate across several Middle Eastern countries, creating potential flashpoints for military confrontation with the United States.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera, supported where available by official military statements. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country outside Iran where US forces conduct strikes against Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026, inclusive. Direct US participation in either unilateral or joint strikes qualifies; threats, proposed operations, and diplomatic support do not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name, or “None” if no qualifying strikes occur.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-26 Day 5-of-8 update (Al Jazeera, Reuters/Khaleej Times, Straits Times, CBS Face the Nation, NYT/CNN): Five of the eight window days (July 22-26) have now elapsed with zero qualifying US strikes outside Iran, leaving only 3 days (July 27-29). Critically, revealed preference in Yemen strongly favors None: even after July 25 Houthi missile/drone attacks on Saudi Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu and a July 26 downed Saudi drone, kinetic strikes inside Yemen remained exclusively Saudi-led coalition / Yemeni Air Force operations rather than US forces. Lifting None 0.52 -> 0.64, trimming Yemen 0.39 -> 0.29 (retaining meaningful risk ahead of PM Netanyahu's Tuesday July 28 White House visit, Trump's 'locked and loaded' posture, and potential Hormuz talks breakdown or further Houthi Red Sea attacks), and trimming Iraq 0.07 -> 0.05 during the proxy lull; Lebanon and Syria remain 0.01 each. Sum = 1.00.

local_articles.title: Red Sea Shipping Slows After Houthi Attack On Saudi Oil Sites, Data Shows
local_articles.snippet: Ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb fell on Sunday after Yemeni Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast, while transit through the Strait of Hormuz stayed low over the weekend, shipping data from Kpler showed on Monday. Eleven commodity vessels passed through the Bab el-Mandeb strait on Sunday, the lowest level in months, the data showed. questions.title: Which country will announce a new multinational maritime coalition to protect navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden by August 1, 2026?
questions.background: Attacks on commercial shipping since 2023 have heightened concerns about the security of maritime trade routes through the Red Sea.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government announcements or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country that announces the creation of a new multinational maritime coalition between July 1 and August 1, 2026, inclusive, with a stated purpose of protecting freedom of navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden. Joining an existing coalition does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-25 update (Reuters/Straits Times, Al Jazeera, Voice of Emirates, BBC): No new multinational Red Sea/Bab al-Mandeb/Gulf of Aden maritime coalition has been announced yet with 4-7 days left, but July 24-25 developments further concentrate pressure on Saudi Arabia. On July 25, Houthi missiles directly targeted Aramco oil sites at Jizan and Yanbu—Saudi Arabia's sole Red Sea export lifeline bypassing the blockaded Strait of Hormuz—while Houthis emphasized their blockade targets Saudi shipping and Riyadh-based GCC called for collective international protection of Bab al-Mandeb. Meanwhile, EU Operation ASPIDES announced new Red Sea/Gulf of Aden commercial escort operations on July 23-24, confirming European states (including France) are operating via existing ASPIDES rather than creating a qualifying new coalition, and the US paused strikes on Iran to pursue Hormuz talks while already leading Prosperity Guardian. Lifting Saudi Arabia 0.53 -> 0.57, holding Egypt at 0.15 (Suez/Red Sea Council stake), trimming United States 0.09 -> 0.08, holding United Kingdom at 0.04, and replacing France (now in residual alongside India, Greece, Djibouti, Italy, China) with United Arab Emirates at 0.03 (major Gulf of Aden/Red Sea maritime footprint and UNSC 2722 statement); sum = 0.87 with 0.13 residual.

questions.title: Which Federal Reserve policymakers will vote for an interest-rate increase at the July 29, 2026 FOMC meeting?
questions.background: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets US monetary policy. Its policy announcements disclose members' votes and the policy preferences of dissenting voters.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Federal Reserve's official policy statement and voting record for the meeting concluding July 29, 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Identify every voting member whose recorded position favors increasing the federal funds target range relative to the range immediately before the meeting. Include those members whether an increase is adopted or they dissent in favor of one. Accepted Answer Format : All qualifying members' surnames, listed alphabetically and separated by commas.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-25 FOMC preview update ahead of the July 28-29 meeting (Fortune July 25, Natixis July 24, FXStreet July 24, Bloomberg/Straits Times July 24): CME FedWatch July 29 hike odds eased from Thursday's 37.9% peak to 34.2% (65.8% hold) as Brent retreated slightly below $100 on Friday and the US paused Iran strikes overnight July 24-25. Crucially, major July 24-25 Wall Street previews converged strongly on a contested HOLD with two hawkish dissents: both TD Securities (Oscar Munoz) and JPMorgan (Michael Feroli) explicitly forecast a hold with at least two hawkish dissents led by Beth Hammack and Lorie Logan, while Natixis (July 24) singled out Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan as the clearest hike dissenter ('perhaps accompanied by Hammack and/or Kashkari') and projected Waller and Cook to join a hold alongside dovish/patient voices Williams and Jefferson (which also lowers the chance of a 12-0 unanimous hike even if Warsh pushes through a rate increase). Lifting modal twin-dissent 'Hammack, Logan' 0.21 -> 0.26, holding the April trio 'Hammack, Kashkari, Logan' at 0.17, raising solo 'Logan' 0.05 -> 0.07 to match trimmed solo 'Hammack' (0.08 -> 0.07), and edging the 12-0 unanimous hike down 0.07 -> 0.06 (sum = 0.63, preserving 0.37 across split majority-hike subsets, 3-4 hawkish dissent blocs including Waller/Bowman, and unanimous hold).

questions.title: Who will succeed Brendon McCullum as permanent head coach of England's men's Test team?
questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution : Resolve to the first person formally appointed as McCullum's permanent successor as head coach of England's men's Test team. Interim appointments and appointments solely concerning limited-overs cricket do not count. Resolution occurs when the appointment is announced, even if the coach begins work later. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Key 2026-07-26 discovery of ESPNcricinfo's July 24 scoop (Matt Roller & Vithushan Ehantharajah, missed in yesterday's scan): ECB managing director Rob Key and an external headhunter made preliminary contact with multiple permanent Test head coach contenders this week—explicitly naming Stephen Fleming, Jonathan Trott, Richard Dawson, and Tom Moody—while noting Marcus Trescothick could deputise on an interim basis for the August 19 Pakistan series (interim appointments do not count). Crucially, this is the second tier-1 ECB-sourced report (matching BBC Sport's July 17 shortlist) to list that exact quartet while omitting Justin Langer, who also retains an LSG IPL schedule clash similar to Andy Flower's. Promoting newly available Stephen Fleming (CSK exit July 13, Rob Key's 2022 top choice, named first by Cricinfo) to solo #1 (0.23 -> 0.27), lifting Jonathan Trott to #2 (0.16 -> 0.19), downgrading Justin Langer sharply from co-#1 to #3 (0.23 -> 0.13, still alive as Cricinfo's list was non-exhaustive), and lifting Richard Dawson (0.08 -> 0.11) and Tom Moody (0.06 -> 0.08), leaving 22% residual for unlisted permanent contenders (e.g., Gareth Batty, Andrew Flintoff, Kumar Sangakkara, permanent Trescothick).

questions.title: Which Southeast Asian country will announce a finalized voluntary repatriation plan for thousands of Myanmar refugees in August 2026?
questions.background: Repatriation means returning refugees to their country of origin. This question concerns finalization of a government plan, rather than the completion of refugee returns.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or reliable news reporting directly quoting those statements. Resolving Event : During August 2026, a Southeast Asian government publicly confirms that it has finalized a voluntary repatriation programme, or the first phase of such a programme, covering at least 1,000 refugees from Myanmar. A preliminary agreement to consider returns is insufficient. Actual departures need not have occurred. Accepted Answer Format : The common English name of the country finalizing the repatriation plan, not the destination country.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-25 update incorporating July 23-24 Malaysia parliamentary breaking news (Reuters/Straits Times, Malay Mail/Bernama, Burma News International, Amnesty Malaysia, The Star): On July 23, Malaysian Deputy Foreign Minister Lukanisman Awang Sauni told the Senate that Malaysia instructed UNHCR to pause refugee registrations during rollout of its domestic DPP system AND disclosed unfinalized plans to repatriate approximately 5,000 Myanmar nationals currently in immigration detention depots by naval vessels 'subject to Myanmar's agreement / the resolution process.' While rights groups and Reuters characterize the naval-ship return as detention deportation rather than a clean voluntary refugee repatriation programme—and Rohingya returns to Rakhine remain obstructed—Putrajaya could finalize and frame a large-scale Myanmar return or companion voluntary repatriation track in August once Naypyidaw agrees, meaningfully lifting Malaysia 0.28 -> 0.36. Thailand remains the clear favorite (trimmed 0.65 -> 0.58) because Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul hosts Min Aung Hlaing in Bangkok on August 6-7 (inside the August window), Thailand hosts ~80,155 registered Myanmar border-camp refugees under an active camp-closure/voluntary-return timeline, and its UNHCR-linked border framework is the cleanest literal match to 'voluntary repatriation.' Indonesia trims 0.04 -> 0.03; Laos and Cambodia hold at 0.01 each (sum = 0.99).
